subject: Private Offer: term architecture & delegated buyer approvals (Acme Retail)
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@acmeretail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Private offer request — pricing, term and approver delegation

Hi Sofia / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is keen to move to a private offer for our piloted apps. Procurement asked me to capture the ask so we can get the right internal approvals in place. High-level:

- Target: Private Offer on AWS Marketplace for Redwood inference HOSTED API (text gen + embeddings).
- Preferred term: 12 months, with an optional 3-month paid pilot to start.
- Expected ARR/commit: ~$180k for year 1 (may split across 3 BU cost centers).
- Approvals: we need delegated buyer approvals — we want an "approver roster" so our three BU leads can sign on behalf of their P&Ls without requiring CFO routing for anything under $250k. For amounts >$250k, CFO signature required.
- Activation: procurement wants options for a 30-day activation window and an escrow holdback clause (5–10%) until basic onboarding milestones are met.

I've attached a rough procurement checklist and their standard PO template (see attachment). Can you send back your recommended private-offer term architecture and any constraints from Redwood side (billing activation, buyer mapping, DocuSign vs Marketplace PO)?

Appreciate quick guidance — procurement would like a proposal by end of week.

Regards,
Samir Shah
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Retail
attachments: acme_po_template.docx (referenced)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private offer request — pricing, term and approver delegation

Team — FYI from Acme (summary below). Need alignment on a defensible structure we can offer quickly. Draft response suggestions:

1) Term architecture
   - Primary: 12-month private offer (committed spend) with monthly usage reporting.
   - Pilot: optional 3-month paid pilot that converts to the remainder of the 12-month term pro-rata if accepted.
   - Early termination: standard AWS Marketplace private-offer activation terms; if pilot fails, revert to pay-as-you-go for remainder.

2) Pricing and escrows
   - Price guidance: for $180k ARR, recommend list discount -> effective net pricing target ~15% off list (Vanessa to confirm).
   - Escrow/holdback: we can accept a 7% holdback retained until onboarding milestones completed (SLA & health-check). Escrow must be explicit in the PO; legal will require language.

3) Buyer approvals / delegation model
   - Proposed mapping: allow up to 3 named approvers (BU leads) to approve POs up to $250k each for that BU. Any single PO >$250k routed to CFO for signature.
   - Activation gating: activation requires signed Marketplace private-offer + PO. For delegated signers we need their name, title and company email to map to the private-offer buyer identity.

4) Activation & timelines
   - Activation window: 30 days from PO submission to activation; we can do a 14-day expedited path if pre-validated finance org is listed.

5) Ops notes
   - We must produce an approval_matrix.xlsx (attached) for their procurement.
   - DocuSign vs Marketplace: prefer Marketplace private-offer acceptance + AWS PO for activation; DocuSign can be used in parallel but Marketplace acceptance is required for immediate activation.

Vanessa — can you confirm the discount banding we can commit to and whether co-sell credits apply? Karthik / Vivek — any objections on 7% holdback? If legal needs different phrasing, we escalate. I'll draft the external reply once aligned.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
S: +1 415 555 0189

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private offer request — pricing, term and approver delegation

Sofia — looks good. Pricing notes:

- For a $180k initial commit across 3 BUs we can offer a 12–16% net discount depending on whether they pick 12 vs 24 months. 12-month = 15% net; 24-month = 18% net (we prefer 12 if they want pilot flexibility).
- Co-sell credits: recommend we apply standard co-sell uplift (if SFDC shows co-sell flagged) — that preserves our margin and helps ACE attainment.
- Holdback: 7% is acceptable; legal will want the milestone definition (onboarding complete = connection live + 2 successful inference jobs).

I agree Marketplace acceptance should be the activation trigger. For delegated buyer approvals, we can map the three BU emails into the private-offer acceptance roster. We should require the CFO only for aggregate spend >$250k per PO.

I'll patch the pricing numbers into the draft and add a short paragraph explaining why 12-month + 3m pilot is lower friction.

-V

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acmeretail.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private offer request — proposed term architecture and approvals

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks — we've put together a proposed structure that should meet procurement constraints while keeping activation fast. See summary below and attached draft private-offer/approval matrix.

Proposed deal structure:
- Offer type: AWS Marketplace Private Offer for Redwood hosted inference (text gen + embeddings).
- Term: 12 months committed, optional 3-month paid pilot that converts pro-rata into the 12 months.
- Pricing: for an expected $180k commit we propose a 15% net discount. If Acme converts to 24 months upfront we can move to 18% net.
- Escrow / Holdback: 7% holdback retained until onboarding milestone (connection live + 2 successful inference jobs). Language included in draft.
- Activation gating: Marketplace private-offer acceptance + Acme PO. We can do expedited activation (14 days) if you provide pre-validated finance contacts.

Buyer approvals and delegation:
- We can map up to 3 named BU approvers to the private-offer; those approvers can approve POs for their BU up to $250k without CFO signature. Any single PO >$250k requires CFO sign-off.
- Please provide the full name, title, and corporate email for each delegated approver and confirm which BU cost center they represent. We will map those identities to the Marketplace buyer roster.

Next steps & timeline:
1) Acme provides approver roster + preferred start date (target start: Jan 4, 2027).
2) We finalize private-offer draft and post it to AWS for approval (we'll share DocuSign link for signature as backup).
3) Once signed and PO is received, do activation and onboarding (target within 30 days).

Attachments: acme_private_offer_draft_v1.pdf, approval_matrix.xlsx

Would you like us to escalate legal on the escrow wording now or wait until you confirm approvers? Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the steps.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@acmeretail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private offer request — proposed term architecture and approvals

Sofia — this looks great, thanks. Procurement reviewed the draft and is comfortable with the 7% holdback and the 12-month + 3-month pilot flow. We will: 

- Send the approver roster (3 names + emails) by EOD Monday 2026-11-22.
- Target start date: Jan 3, 2027 with pilot running Jan–Mar.
- Procurement will issue PO using our template; please confirm final DocuSign link and HubSpot deal id so we can reference it on the PO.

One quick ask: can you include the HubSpot deal id (if available) in the private-offer notes so AWS can link activation to the correct sales record?

I'll loop in Priya and procurement once we send approvers.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Retail
